runners_data.name: Peckedbytheparrott
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way on his only start at the Curragh after a tardy exit from the stalls, though he plugged on to finish fifth; a good deal of improvement is needed if he is to factor here.

runners_data.name: Cochise County
runners_data.comment: Matched a modest debut level when well beaten here on his latest start and faces a tough task again at this venue; the breeding points towards shorter trips, so 6-7f may be more his territory in time, but more is required at this level.

runners_data.name: September Duke
runners_data.comment: A 25,000-euro Sergei Prokofiev colt who is a half-brother to Degale, a useful performer at a mile, and has top jockey support on debut; others among the first-timers appear to have stronger credentials, though the pedigree suggests he may progress with experience.

runners_data.name: Ballyskeagh
runners_data.comment: A 42,000-euro Gleneagles filly who is a half-sister to Port Light, a smart performer at a mile, and comes with the backing of a trainer with an excellent record here; she commands respect for her first start and the pedigree gives confidence the trip will suit.

runners_data.name: Elyatta
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way in an auction race at Fairyhouse on his only start, never really getting into contention from a rear position; the stable has a strong record in this race and he looks the type to improve when he gets into handicap company.

runners_data.name: Seaxburh
runners_data.comment: Caught the eye with a promising debut at this track, beaten 3 lengths in an auction race here and running on to suggest there is more to offer; a top trainer with an excellent record at this venue can draw more from her at the second attempt.

runners_data.name: Whosinterviewinwho
runners_data.comment: A 10,000-euro Inns Of Court colt with a dam who showed decent ability at 7f as a juvenile; he looks likely to need more experience before becoming competitive, and the overall picture points to this being one to follow rather than support on debut.

runners_data.name: Damsel In Distress
runners_data.comment: Struggled to get into it on her only start at Listowel after a tardy beginning, finishing well beaten, but the breeding pointing to 7f and beyond suggests a more suitable test awaits; she will need to find more to compete here but improvement is anticipated.

runners_data.name: Banks Of The Boyne
runners_data.comment: Showed gradual progress from the rear after a sluggish start on his debut at Fairyhouse, finishing 8 lengths back, but was closing towards the finish and the breeding suggests 7f and further will suit; he is expected to come on for that initial experience.

runners_data.name: Buck Jones
runners_data.comment: A 7,000-euro Elzaam gelding whose half-brother Stepinmydirection showed useful ability at 7f, and the stable has a strong record in this race; he is probably best kept in mind for a future outing, as the overall profile suggests he needs this first start to furnish experience.

runners_data.name: Nando Royale
runners_data.comment: Beaten just over 5 lengths on his debut at Fairyhouse but the trip was likely too short given his breeding for 7f and beyond, and the step up in distance today looks a clear positive; he can improve for that run and has leading-danger claims.

runners_data.name: Oristown Boy
runners_data.comment: A step forward from his debut when fourth at Down Royal, beaten just a length over 7f on soft ground, confirming he handles the conditions well; he keeps his form consistently and is fully capable of running a big race here.

runners_data.name: Jezzie Bea
runners_data.comment: A 20,000-euro Oscar Performance filly who is a half-sister to Master Of Zest, a smart performer at 7f, and her yard has taken 2 of the last 10 renewals of this race; she is taken seriously for her debut and the pedigree suggests the trip will suit.

runners_data.name: Magna Fortuna
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way on her only start at Fairyhouse on debut, and the assessment is that she needs more time before she is ready to compete at this level; she remains of interest for the future but asks too much today.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Rain
runners_data.comment: Ran a bold race at Leopardstown on her latest start, beaten only a nose in second, and confirms she handles 7f well on a sound surface; with first-time cheekpieces added today, she has strong claims on that evidence.

runners_data.name: Docks
runners_data.comment: Out of contention from the outset after a very sluggish start at Leopardstown on his only run, finishing down the field, and will need a major step forward to get involved here; hard to make a case for him at this stage.

runners_data.name: Caoch The Piper
runners_data.comment: Beaten down the field from an off-the-pace position at Down Royal on her most recent start and has plenty to find at this level; the breeding does point to a mile being her best trip in time, but more is needed here to get involved.

runners_data.name: Supreme Act
runners_data.comment: Beaten 6 lengths on his debut at Down Royal in an auction race, and a forward step is both anticipated and needed if he is to get competitive here; he has the profile of a colt capable of improving as the season progresses.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden

runners_data.name: Almeiyda
runners_data.comment: Fourth on her most recent start at Gowran Park, running to form despite showing some keenness, and the drop in trip looks an enticing switch for a filly effective at this distance; her connections have landed this race before, though the short break is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Black Chicken
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way on her only start at Gowran Park, making no impression from the rear of the field, and will need to find a great deal more to get competitive here.

runners_data.name: Bofa Beach
runners_data.comment: Handles the trip and ground well and the return to a shorter distance after failing to stay further at Gowran Park looks a clear plus; she showed the ability to finish third earlier in her campaign, with consistency being the main question.

runners_data.name: Ebony Reign
runners_data.comment: A step back from her debut level at the Curragh on her most recent outing, finishing down the field, but there could be untapped improvement to come and she wears a tongue-tie for the first time; the profile suggests she has more to offer.

runners_data.name: Ellens Bay
runners_data.comment: Returning from a lengthy absence after finishing down the field at Dundalk on her most recent start, and will need to find considerably more on that evidence to play a part here; she does handle the all-weather surface, though faces a stiff task.

runners_data.name: Elusive Echo
runners_data.comment: Showed genuine promise on her debut at Gowran Park, finishing a close third over a mile on yielding ground, and adds a tongue-tie today with a trainer who has an excellent record at this course; a filly with the scope to take a step forward.

runners_data.name: Haroussa
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on her only start at Naas and substantial improvement is required to make an impression here; her trainer is currently in good form and the breeding, with the dam successful at 7f, suggests longer trips may suit better in time.

runners_data.name: Miss Moore Cen
runners_data.comment: A step forward from her debut effort when fifth at Down Royal most recently, suggesting she handles this trip on good ground; still some way short of a competitive level, but the upward trend from her early starts is encouraging.

runners_data.name: Moon Aura
runners_data.comment: Performed to her usual level at Gowran Park on her latest outing, beaten around four and a half lengths in a handicap, and tries first-time cheekpieces today in a bid to find improvement; she handles this distance well but needs to find more to get competitive.

runners_data.name: Reap The Rewards
runners_data.comment: Beaten well on her only start at the Curragh, where she appeared to struggle with the testing ground conditions, but returns from a break with first-time cheekpieces today and her effort at 7f suggested she can do better on sounder going.

runners_data.name: Spring Sprinter
runners_data.comment: Matched her debut level at Gowran Park most recently, held comfortably in the latter half of the field, and the shorter trip today looks a negative for her profile; the trainer is also in a lean spell at present.

runners_data.name: Star Of Beauty
runners_data.comment: A close second at Gowran Park on her latest start, finishing just half a length adrift over a mile, and she handles varied going across a range of trips; now adding a first-time visor with the top course jockey aboard, she has genuine claims.

runners_data.name: Storm Petrel
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way on her only start at Naas and is returning from a very lengthy absence, making assessment difficult; she will need a dramatic improvement to get involved here.

runners_data.name: Wildlife
runners_data.comment: Beaten around 10 lengths on her debut at Gowran Park but did display a hint of ability in the process; she needs to find considerably more to make an impact here and improvement is clearly required.

races.name: Jimmy Murray Agri Services Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Blue Anthem
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid Good-ground form and Shane Foley booked; 43 days off may mean a fitness question but the 6/15 similar-going record shows capability, and the tongue-tie is retained — well positioned to track Eichan San and strike.|
runners_data.comment: Had plenty to contend with last time here, missing the break and encountering traffic, leaving him with ground impossible to recover; he now tries a first-time tongue-tie and is effective at shorter distances on sound surfaces. A bounce back in form is needed after a string of disappointing efforts.

runners_data.name: Brains
runners_data.note: Veteran ten-year-old who has shown Good-ground form recently (ran 2nd at 8f on Good), Seamie Heffernan is a major upgrade in the saddle; naturally prominent and should get a good tow into the race if he travels sweetly.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten six and a half lengths at Gowran Park on his most recent start but had run creditably in the two previous outings, including a runner-up placing; he steps out in first-time tongue-tie and blinkers. Winless in recent starts, he is capable over this trip and ground.

runners_data.name: Methgal
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who has shown consistency over this course-and-distance range on Good ground, though hasn't won yet at this level; Conor Cusack's 7lb claim helps the weight, and the tongue-tie is a positive, but the 0/2 trainer 14-day record is minor concern.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Limerick last time, going down by two lengths off this precise mark, which looks like a solid recent effort; first-time tongue-tie and blinkers are added today as connections seek to extract more. He won earlier this year and leads our ratings with the mark in his favour.

runners_data.name: Givehertilxmas
runners_data.note: 168-day absence is a significant flag for this hold-up type from a handler with a quiet 0/2 recent record; no similar-going wins or places on record, and stepping back to 7½f after a long break makes this a risky proposition.|
runners_data.comment: Has form at seven to eight furlongs with cut in the ground but was keyed up and well beaten when stretched to 11f at Dundalk last time; today's shorter trip is more suitable, though 168 days off adds to the uncertainty.

runners_data.name: La La Lucrative
runners_data.note: Won a 7f handicap on Good ground recently so the conditions are right, but flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — the hold-up style requires a strong late surge, which the fade tendency undermines; could show early without lasting.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a win two runs ago and handles the trip well on a variety of ground; he lines up 1lb lower than at his most recent defeat and the mark looks manageable. Inconsistency has been an issue, but a good day could see him go close.

runners_data.name: Medieval Night
runners_data.note: Hold-up type dropping in distance from 9f-plus, which could unlock some tactical speed; Chris Hayes is a quality rider and the 12-day turnaround suggests yard has him ready, though the Good-ground form (0W2P) confirms he has never won on this surface.|
runners_data.comment: Third at Leopardstown on his latest start, going down by four and a quarter lengths in a solid display; he handles today's trip and ground and steps out in first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces. Winless in recent starts, there is enough to respect here if those aids bring improvement.

runners_data.name: The Blue Panther
runners_data.note: A true hold-up runner at heart, but the redistribution note is relevant — forced into a midfield role by the volume of hold-up horses, meaning he won't get his natural position; the fade flag and STYLE_FIT of 0.92 both dampen enthusiasm.|
runners_data.comment: Won over this sort of trip earlier in the season and tends to do his best work from the front, but form has tailed off sharply since with two unplaced efforts; first-time cheekpieces are added today and a return to his earlier level is the aim.

runners_data.name: Shahada Ace
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good ground but has since run 9th, 9th, and 6th; the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) reflects that as a true hold-up type he'll be racing out of role today, and the 56-day gap adds an element of doubt about peak fitness.|
runners_data.comment: Won over a mile on her best distance but has struggled since, including a poor effort at Gowran Park where she was too free early; she returns here after a short break still 3lb above her last successful mark, and sound going at least plays to her strengths.

runners_data.name: Toy Soldier
runners_data.note: Ran 2nd at 7f on Soft recently which shows form is there, but the headgear (visor) suggests a tendency to need motivation; mapped away from his natural trailing position and the STYLE_FIT (0.90) flag means he's unlikely to reproduce that effort from midfield.|
runners_data.comment: A half-length second at Down Royal last time off a 2lb lower mark, his most promising recent effort; he tries a first-time visor and the mark looks fair based on that form. Without a win in recent starts, he could be competitive if he builds on that showing.

runners_data.name: Snap Decision
runners_data.note: Little recent form to recommend here — three consecutive poor runs with an 87-day layoff; the redistribution note applies and the fade warning compounds what is already a speculative profile; needs everything to go right.|
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in each of his last four starts, including a distant effort at Cork, and now returns after a near three-month absence; bred for six to eight furlongs and stamina over this trip is unproven. His first handicap run offers a degree of scope, but more is needed.

runners_data.name: Alandownunder
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a consistent record of finishing 8th-10th on Good ground, and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) reflects that this natural hold-up type will be forced wide of his comfort zone; the blinkers are first-time equipment but past form offers little encouragement.|
runners_data.comment: Well below maiden level at Fairyhouse most recently, consistent with her recent pattern of struggling at the back of the field; she tries first-time blinkers here and the pedigree suggests a requirement for at least seven furlongs. More improvement is needed before she can feature.

runners_data.name: Polanco
runners_data.note: Form reads 15-12-14-8-13 which tells its own story; a hold-up horse mapped into midfield and flagged as a fader, with no wins from five Good-ground runs — the redistribution away from his preferred position makes a first win here very unlikely.|
runners_data.comment: Struggled in each of his last five outings, including a well-beaten effort at the Curragh most recently; he now tries a first-time tongue-tie and handles seven furlongs. Improvement is needed before he can feature, even in handicap company at this level.

runners_data.name: Misava
runners_data.note: 364-day absence is an enormous flag for any horse, let alone one from a trainer with a 0/4 recent return; only three career runs, all finishing 8th-16th, and the redistribution from true hold-up to midfield simply adds another layer of difficulty.|
runners_data.comment: Returns after a near-year absence, having been unable to make any impact on her last three starts, the most recent here at Roscommon; she steps out in a first-time hood which may help. A significant step up from previous form is needed to feature in this field.

runners_data.name: Queen Of Newark
runners_data.note: Ran 3rd over 8f on Good ground which offers a modest glimmer, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) and the fade warning make her hard to back; a three-year-old filly dropped back from 8f who'll be doing her best work at the wrong end.|
runners_data.comment: Third two runs ago but well beaten at Down Royal on her most recent start, unable to build on that effort; effective over seven furlongs and has form at today's track. Without a win in recent starts, a return to that earlier level is what she needs.

runners_data.name: He's Holding Court
runners_data.note: Ran 4th at 8f on Good recently which is encouraging form proximity, but the redistribution from hold-up to midfield disrupts his ability to produce a late challenge; at 119lbs he's well weighted but the tactical disruption is a significant obstacle.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth at this course on her latest outing, going down by seven and a quarter lengths but showing enough to be respected; effective over seven to eight furlongs and returns after a short break. Without a win in recent starts, she looks open to improvement and warrants consideration.

runners_data.name: Selective Power
runners_data.note: Top-rated alongside Blue Anthem and Eichan San on OR=60 and has recent 4th and 4th placings on Good ground at 8f; hold-up style is genuine but Roscommon 7½f requires getting competitive sooner than he'd naturally like — could be involved if the pace tests.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Gowran Park last time, going down by two lengths off this exact mark in a consistent effort; he handles a variety of going and is suited by today's seven to eight furlongs. First-time cheekpieces are added today and a repeat performance would make him competitive.

runners_data.name: Zheleznaya Dama
runners_data.note: Ran 3rd at 7f on Good ground which is relevant course-and-distance form, and the 16-day turnaround looks intentional; no jockey listed is a concern, and the recent P (pulled up) in the form string needs explaining before taking the 7½f trip on trust.|
runners_data.comment: Something appeared to be amiss when she was pulled up in a handicap at Cork last time; two runs prior she had finished third, and she handles seven furlongs. That experience leaves a question mark and fitness needs to be established before she can be backed with confidence.

runners_data.name: Eichan San
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner and likely leader, though the STYLE_FIT (0.93) tag reflects he's not a natural frontrunner and the 0/7 trainer 14-day record is poor; sets his own fractions in a big field but the question is whether he can sustain his effort over 7½f.|
runners_data.comment: Badly away at Leopardstown last time and could not recover, beaten nine lengths after a tardy break; first-time blinkers are added today which should help sharpen his concentration from the stalls. Suited by six to seven furlongs, he has a chance here if he can get away cleanly.

races.paceDynamic: Eichan San is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner 0-60 handicap over 7½f at Roscommon and is likely to stride into an uncontested lead from the off, setting a measured, sustainable gallop on Good ground. Blue Anthem, Brains, and Methgal will press forward into prominent positions just behind, creating a small cluster of early pace without any genuine challenger looking to harry Eichan San for the lead. The field holds significantly more prominent and hold-up types than can all secure their natural position — Blue Anthem, Brains, and Methgal are best placed to get prominent berths, while Alandownunder, The Blue Panther, Polanco, and others who would naturally want to race prominently will be shuffled back into midfield against their instincts. With a lone front-runner controlling proceedings at a moderate tempo on a flat track, this race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently from the outset and have the stamina to sustain their effort, giving those travelling just behind Eichan San the optimal platform to pounce in the straight.

scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Eichan San leads unchallenged at a controlled pace and the prominent trio cannot sustain a challenge from 2f out.
scenarios.body: If Eichan San leads unchallenged at a controlled pace and the prominent trio cannot sustain a challenge from 2f out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Anthem or Brains track Eichan San closely and have enough in reserve to collar him inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Blue Anthem or Brains track Eichan San closely and have enough in reserve to collar him inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady and a horse in the mid-division gets a dream passage down the centre to pick off the leaders.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely steady and a horse in the mid-division gets a dream passage down the centre to pick off the leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Burst From Deep
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses dramatically and hold-up horses get a clear run to deliver a late charge.
scenarios.body: If the early pace collapses dramatically and hold-up horses get a clear run to deliver a late charge.

watchPoints.text: Eichan San needs monitoring from the stalls — if he doesn't break cleanly in this 18-runner field, the uncontested lead evaporates and the entire pace map reshapes significantly.

Blue Anthem and Brains are both likely to hunt down early positions aggressively; a scrimmage for the prominent spots in the first furlong could compromise one or both, particularly with 18 runners over the Roscommon chute start.

La La Lucrative won on Good ground recently and could be underrated at a price, but the fade flag is important — watch whether Robbie Colgan asks her to improve position earlier than ideal, which could expose the tendency to tie up.

Medieval Night is stepping down sharply in distance (was running over 9-14f) and Chris Hayes may exploit any pace collapse in the straight — flag if the early tempo is slower than expected and he travels sweetly into the race.

Zheleznaya Dama has no jockey confirmed in the data and has a pulled-up run in recent form — track the declaration and jockey booking, as any last-minute rider change could affect how the hold-up tactics are deployed.

races.name: Conor Cassidy Car Sales Handicap

runners_data.name: Iamimmaculate
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner who will be allowed a soft lead; 255 days off is a significant fitness query for Gerard O'Leary's 3yo, and the step up to 1m2½f on Good ground is untested, but the uncontested lead is a major tactical asset.
runners_data.comment: Shaped promisingly when a half-length second at Leopardstown off a 4lb lower mark last autumn, and showed a win in him before that, but 255 days off means a fitness question on return. Effective over six to eight furlongs, the current mark is a stiffer ask.

runners_data.name: Adel
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Good last time for M D O'Callaghan, giving it the strongest form claim at this trip in this field; hold-up style suits a strongly-run race and the 43-day break appears no concern given that recent win.
runners_data.comment: Landed a 12f handicap at this course last time, getting the better by a half-length, and tops our ratings heading into this. He is well suited by sound ground, though stamina at ten furlongs is the slight unknown coming back in trip.

runners_data.name: Honouramongthieves
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type who has been placed at 8f on Heavy but has shown little at 12f on Good or Soft; form figures of 7-6-6 at this trip suggest the horse struggles to quicken at this distance.
runners_data.comment: Showed decent form earlier in the season and stays ten furlongs, but his best efforts have come with give in the ground; today's conditions may not be ideal. Well held at Newbury on his most recent start, a change in direction is required.

runners_data.name: Nermal
runners_data.note: Ben Coen's mount for Andrew Slattery, who has sent out three winners in the last 28 days; Nermal is placed on each of its last three starts and races prominently, giving it an ideal tactical position to track the leader and strike in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Third at Ballinrobe on his latest outing and has placed in three of his last four starts; he looks open to further progress and handles today's trip and ground well. This is his first try in a handicap, which brings an element of the unknown.

runners_data.name: Rapide Vega
runners_data.note: Placed last time over 10f on Good for trainer Harrington, who is in excellent current form; a genuine hold-up runner wearing a hood, and the step up to 1m2½f looks within range given that effort.
runners_data.comment: Second at Gowran Park on his latest outing, beaten twelve lengths but claiming the runner-up spot, and now fitted with first-time cheekpieces in a bid to improve; effective over today's trip and going. The mark looks workable and he could be competitive if that headgear brings the desired sharpening.

runners_data.name: Freedom And Light
runners_data.note: Bolger's 3yo has finished in the frame at 10f on Good but has a poor recent run of form (9-8-4-6-7); although a natural hold-up type, it is pushed into a midfield slot here and that compromises the late run this horse needs.
runners_data.comment: Well held in recent outings and last time was caught flat-footed out of the stalls at Leopardstown, leaving her with too much ground to make up; effective at ten furlongs on yielding ground, a clean break is a prerequisite for any chance here.

runners_data.name: Vantage Code
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins' gelding has six consecutive defeats and has never placed beyond 9f; a true hold-up runner forced into midfield by a crowded rear, making its chance of breaking a losing run slender.
runners_data.comment: Trailing the field at Down Royal on his most recent outing after failing to land a blow off the pace; five outings without a placing in recent starts and improvement is clearly needed. Some stamina in the breeding at least gives hope over this trip.

runners_data.name: Second Line
runners_data.note: Harrington's second runner wears a hood and has a finish-fade flag; the horse's natural style is at the rear, but with the map full it operates from midfield — a combination of the hood and the fading tendency makes this a difficult profile to back.
runners_data.comment: Struggled when asked to go beyond ten furlongs at Limerick last time; today's drop back in trip looks a positive, and he arrives in first-time blinkers which could help. Winless in recent starts, he remains capable on his best form over this distance on a surface he handles.

runners_data.name: Dont Get Me Wrong
runners_data.note: A prominent racer for Gerard O'Leary who carries a finish-fade flag; won over 7f on Standard but this is a 1m2½f turf handicap on Good ground with a stiff finish, and the fade warning makes it hard to see this horse lasting home.
runners_data.comment: Won at shorter trips earlier but well held since, including a distant last here when unable to make any impression having been held up; the step up to 10f brings a stamina query, and he returns after a short break.

runners_data.name: Ella's Gold
runners_data.note: Wesley Joyce (3lb claim) on a Matthew Smith-trained filly who has been placed five times without winning; races prominently and the 19-day turnaround is normal, with the 9f Soft effort last time suggesting this trip and ground are within range.
runners_data.comment: Placed at Leopardstown last time, beaten just a half-length off a 2lb lower mark, pointing to a return to her best after a poor run before that; effective on today's going, she makes a strong appeal as a danger despite yet to score in recent starts.

races.paceDynamic: Iamimmaculate is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground over 1m2½f at Roscommon. Nermal, Dont Get Me Wrong, and Ella's Gold are the prominent types most likely to press from behind, while the hold-up contingent — Adel, Honouramongthieves, and Rapide Vega — will settle in the rear third waiting on a finishing kick. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear: Vantage Code, Freedom And Light, and Second Line are genuine closers who are unlikely to find their natural position and will instead be crowded into midfield, blunting their effectiveness. An uncontested, measured lead from Iamimmaculate on Good ground over this trip sets up a race where the pace is honest but not brutal — tactically, this shape favours horses who can race prominently just behind the leader and sustain their effort into the straight, rather than those relying on a late burst from an unfavoured rear position.

scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Iamimmaculate dictates an uncontested, even gallop and the prominent runners behind track efficiently into the straight.
scenarios.body: If Iamimmaculate dictates an uncontested, even gallop and the prominent runners behind track efficiently into the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly strong enough to compromise front-runners and a genuine hold-up type finds a clear run in the straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace is truly strong enough to compromise front-runners and a genuine hold-up type finds a clear run in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Iamimmaculate sets a deceptively strong early tempo that causes prominent runners to come off the bridle before the straight.
scenarios.body: If Iamimmaculate sets a deceptively strong early tempo that causes prominent runners to come off the bridle before the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Fade, Midfield Steals
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so moderate that the race turns into a sprint finish from the home turn, with midfield types catching the leaders flat-footed.
scenarios.body: If the pace is so moderate that the race turns into a sprint finish from the home turn, with midfield types catching the leaders flat-footed.

watchPoints.text: Iamimmaculate has been off the track for 255 days — watch for any signs of ring-rustiness in the pre-parade or at the start, as fitness failure here collapses the entire race shape.

Adel, Honouramongthieves, and Rapide Vega are all genuine hold-up types hunting the same stretch of late ground; watch for traffic problems in the straight if they all converge on the same gap simultaneously.

Nermal has posted three consecutive placed efforts and is in the care of a trainer with three winners in 14 days — watch for Ben Coen tracking Iamimmaculate closely from flag fall, which would signal a live prominent challenge.

Second Line and Dont Get Me Wrong both carry finish-fade flags — watch whether either horse is still travelling at the two-furlong pole, as fading before that point would confirm the pace has been stronger than it appeared.

Freedom And Light and Vantage Code, both true hold-up types displaced into midfield, are worth monitoring for positioning at the start — if either jockey elects to drop out to their natural rear position regardless, it may signal an outside market move.

races.name: Sean Cleary Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Sonoran
runners_data.note: Hold-up type trained by G M Lyons, placed on Good going over 9f recently (sim-going 0W 2P from 9 runs), but stepping up in trip to 10f at Roscommon in a race where the rear of the field will be crowded — needs things to go right late.
runners_data.comment: Held comfortably in a handicap at Leopardstown last time in a run below his best, he carries first-time tongue-tie from stall 10. He handles today's trip and conditions and the trainer is in good form, though a turnaround from that display is needed.

runners_data.name: Amplitude
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with recent form in this distance range (12f–13f), but 43 days off and trainer showing no 14-day form; sim-going record of 0W 2P from 11 tries on Good suggests placed rather than winning profile.
runners_data.comment: Third here on his most recent start, finishing 4½ lengths off the pace in a handicap, he has rediscovered his form and handles the course, trip and going ideally. A consistent performer who should run another solid race from stall 7.

runners_data.name: Liam Swagger
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, due to set sole fractions — but 422 days absent is a significant fitness flag; won twice at this distance on Soft/Yielding and his style fits the role perfectly, yet the layoff could compromise his ability to sustain his lead in the closing stages.
runners_data.comment: Placed at Newmarket in his final British start, beaten 3¼ lengths off a marginally higher mark, he now tries first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces from stall 3 on return from a long absence. Effective up to 14f on a sound surface, though much is asked on his Irish debut.

runners_data.name: Follow Me
runners_data.note: Carries a hold-up profile (hg:p) but recent form over shorter trips (7f–8f) than today's 10f; DBM in the saddle is a major positive, though sim-going record of 1W 1P from 15 runs on Good suggests he rarely wins on this surface.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 6½ lengths here last time in a handicap over today's trip, he now adds first-time cheekpieces from stall 4. He handles this course and distance and there is reason to believe he can do better, though he has been out of the frame in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Unterberg
runners_data.note: Progressive prominent type who has won three of his last four starts, all on Stanmore going — the switch to Good turf at Roscommon is a query, but his course-distance profile and front-rank style make him ideally placed to exploit Swagger if the leader fades; 88 days off is the only mild concern.
runners_data.comment: Three consecutive victories before a poor run at Lingfield last time, from which he returns to turf off a competitive mark from stall 6. His earlier form demonstrates he handles today's conditions and he looks capable of bouncing back here.

runners_data.name: Vlhova
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong form over shorter trips (7f–8f), stepping up to 10f after a 237-day absence — the extra distance is untested and the layoff is notable; Shane Foley booked is a positive, but Stanmore form (0W 1P on Good sim) warrants caution.
runners_data.comment: A consistent performer who went down by three-quarters of a length at Dundalk last time, she is effective at a mile and handles today's ground well. Returning from a lengthy absence from stall 12 is the main question, but her form line is solid.

runners_data.name: Grey Leader
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a modest recent record (50-008), back quickly after 8 days and trainer carrying a 14-day flag; sim-going record of 1W 1P from 15 Good-ground runs suggests occasional big days but not consistently.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a handicap at Ballinrobe just eight days ago in another disappointing effort, he draws stall 1 and handles today's trip and going. He has the ability to perform better than his recent starts suggest, but is an unreliable conveyance.

runners_data.name: Marta's Prince
runners_data.note: Style unknown — limited data available with only three runs in the history and a 234-day absence; trained by R P Burns (same yard as Grey Leader), form figure of a win last season gives some hope but the long break and unknown style make this very hard to assess.
runners_data.comment: Seventh at Chantilly latest in a run below his best, he returns from an absence of over seven months to this company from stall 9. He won a claimer at Clairefontaine last August and is effective at 7-9f, but this looks considerably harder.

runners_data.name: Sir Jeremy
runners_data.note: Active Noel Meade yard (T14: 2/8) and a winner on Good over 10f in recent form, but his natural hold-up style means he has been pushed into a midfield slot by the weight of closers in this field — if he can't get his usual rear berth, his finishing kick will be blunted.
runners_data.comment: Ninth last time, failing to land a blow at this trip off the same mark he carries today, he is most effective on a sound surface, which is a minor concern. He has the ability to show considerably more but needs a sharper effort.

runners_data.name: Thatwilldoso
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who ran only 8 days ago; best form is over 10f–13f and the sim-going record of 3W 6P from 15 Good/Soft starts is the strongest in the field on this surface — front-rank position suits, though the quick turnaround is worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: She landed this race 12 months ago and remains progressive over today's trip with plenty of cut, but was beaten nine lengths at Ballinrobe just eight days ago, struggling for pace. Her mark is gradually easing and she could step forward, but a turnaround is needed.

runners_data.name: Sinbad My Dad
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up type forced to race closer to the pace than ideal given the crowded closer's group; 158-day absence and apprentice booking (Joseph Harnett, 7lb) add risk, and the Stanmore form (1W 1P from 15 STA runs) doesn't fully translate to Good turf.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a handicap at Dundalk on his most recent start, failing to see out the distance, he returns from around five months off to a shorter trip that should suit better. He handles today's conditions and has shown fair form in similar company.

runners_data.name: Flying Fortress
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning after 18 days for Gavin Cromwell (T14: 1/19 — strong trainer form); hg:b (blinkers) fitted and best recent form over 10f on Good, making him a natural tracker of Swagger — the blinkers could sharpen him for a challenge in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 4¼ lengths at Gowran Park last time in a run over a shorter trip, he goes in first-time blinkers here and handles today's conditions over this distance. He is on a competitive mark and has the profile to feature, though the trainer's current record is a note of caution.

runners_data.name: Blackjack Hills
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse tagged as fading in the finish, squeezed into a midfield slot by the field's closer-heavy composition — after 237 days off and without a win on Good ground in three tries (0W 0P on sim), the combination of long absence, out-of-role placement, and a known tendency to fade makes this a speculative chance at best.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins going into this return from a long absence, including landing a handicap at Dundalk by three-quarters of a length off a lower mark, confirm a progressive trend. He handles today's distance and conditions, and goes from stall 11 on a mark above his last winning level.

races.paceDynamic: Liam Swagger is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field and, with no horse willing or able to seriously contest the lead, is set to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested tempo over this 1m2½f trip on Good ground at Roscommon. Behind him, Unterberg, Vlhova, Thatwilldoso, and Flying Fortress will vie for prominent positions, but with several hold-up types also in the field — Sir Jeremy, Sinbad My Dad, and Blackjack Hills — the midfield and rear will be congested, with those redistributed horses unlikely to secure their natural position at the back. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate; Sir Jeremy, Sinbad My Dad, and Blackjack Hills are genuine closers but will be shuffled into a midfield role by circumstance, diluting their finish. A single, uncontested lead at an honest-but-not-suicidal clip on a flat, Good-ground track overwhelmingly favours prominent racers who can track and pounce, rather than true closers who will find themselves neither in front nor with the room to come from behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Swagger Leads, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Liam Swagger dictates a controlled solo lead and prominent horses track comfortably into the straight.
scenarios.body: If Liam Swagger dictates a controlled solo lead and prominent horses track comfortably into the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Swagger Fades
scenarios.trigger: If Liam Swagger's 422-day absence causes him to tire in the straight, gifting the race to the first wave of chasers.
scenarios.body: If Liam Swagger's 422-day absence causes him to tire in the straight, gifting the race to the first wave of chasers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Thread Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow, compressing the field and allowing lightly covered midfielders to weave through in the straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely slow, compressing the field and allowing lightly covered midfielders to weave through in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Hold-Ups Overcome Disadvantage
scenarios.trigger: If Sir Jeremy, Sinbad My Dad, or Blackjack Hills find clear daylight and produce a sustained late run despite racing out of their natural role.
scenarios.body: If Sir Jeremy, Sinbad My Dad, or Blackjack Hills find clear daylight and produce a sustained late run despite racing out of their natural role.

watchPoints.text: Liam Swagger's 422-day absence is the pivotal fitness question — if he ties up in the final furlong, the race is blown wide open for the prominent trackers immediately behind him, making Unterberg and Flying Fortress dangerous.

Unterberg has won three of his last four but all on Stanmore going — watch for any signs of him finding Good turf at Roscommon an entirely different surface, particularly on a flat track that rewards a genuine stride.

The weight of hold-up types — Sir Jeremy, Sinbad My Dad, Blackjack Hills, Sonoran, Amplitude — all trying to close from a congested midfield creates a real risk of a traffic problem in the straight; watch for any runner getting boxed in at a critical point.

Flying Fortress runs in blinkers for Gavin Cromwell, whose 14-day strike rate (1/19) flags stable form — the headgear change in a race where a prominent position is freely available makes him a horse to monitor early in running.

Thatwilldoso has the best surface-specific record in the field (3W 6P from 15 Good/Soft runs) and ran only 8 days ago — quick turnarounds can suit fit horses in handicap company, and his proximity to the pace in a race with one lone front-runner is a tactical advantage worth noting.

races.name: Watch Racing TV Irish EBF Lenebane Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Chally Chute
runners_data.note: A genuine stalker whose OR 112 heads this field on official ratings; Donagh O'Connor gives this yard an in-form partnership angle, and 11 days since a winning run on good ground at 12f is ideal preparation — the trip step-up to 1m4f looks straightforward based on a 16f win at Healey's Hotel.
runners_data.comment: A fine effort in a Listed race at Limerick last time, going down by half a length after finishing with good late energy over this trip, confirms he is in excellent heart. He landed this race 12 months ago and has every chance of going close again.

runners_data.name: Starford
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's stable is firing at 10/74 over 14 days and Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking elevates this runner's claims; 53 days off since a run in heavier conditions is a mild flag, but his OR 111 and a win at 11f on heavy suggest he handles ease underfoot — good here is not a confirmed concern, merely untested at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a Group 2 at Chester last time after being asked to make up too much ground, he is better judged on his earlier form, having landed a race earlier in the campaign. The trainer has a strong record at this venue and Starford is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Counting Coup
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won on soft 10 days ago over 13f and has a clear intent to lead from tape to tape under Leigh Roche; faces an equally determined Dreamkeeper for the early lead, meaning he is unlikely to get a soft time out front — his stamina at 1m4f good ground is a question given his limited profile (2 runs only).
runners_data.comment: Won a maiden at Down Royal on his Flat debut by three lengths last time and showed clear ability on that occasion, but this is a considerably tougher assignment and he needs to find considerably more in this grade.

runners_data.name: Shaool
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes over on a horse that has won on good ground at 12f and carries the headgear notation (p); JP Murtagh's yard is in decent form at 6/29, and while OR 104 makes Shaool the class second-string, his pattern of running big in-between defeats (211 form) gives legitimate each-way appeal in a truly-run contest.
runners_data.comment: A Group 2 at the Curragh last time saw her beaten close to 10 lengths when running to handicap level, but the trainer is in good form and she reappears in first-time cheekpieces. Effective over today's trip with plenty of give in the ground, she is respected.

runners_data.name: Abbey Actress
runners_data.note: Comes here in the form of her life having won last time on soft over 10f, but her true style is prominent — in a field already packed with horses wanting that position, she is likely racing further back than ideal; the Murtagh yard double-handed is worth noting, and good ground (0 wins from 2 on GOO) is a mild query.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap at Leopardstown comfortably last time and is effective over today's trip and conditions, she now goes in first-time cheekpieces. The step up in grade makes this considerably harder, and the trainer's recent form is a concern.

runners_data.name: Bosphorus Rose
runners_data.note: Her best form is on good ground at 12f (won) and she drops back from a 3rd here 16 days ago in the same conditions, giving her strong course-and-distance claims; her natural racing style is up with the pace, but with the lead slots already taken she will be forced to track from midfield — that positional compromise tempers confidence despite the obvious course form.
runners_data.comment: Third in a Group 3 at Cork on her most recent start, she has the quality to be competitive here and handles any going at this trip. The stable has a fine record in this event and she has a top course rider in the saddle — a genuine danger.

runners_data.name: Kalixa
runners_data.note: Returning from a 271-day absence for O'Callaghan, whose stable has 0 wins from 13 runners in the past fortnight — a significant negative angle; her one win came on good ground over 10f and nothing in her profile suggests she can produce a career-best off this layoff at Listed level, making her an outsider regardless of scenario.
runners_data.comment: Third in a conditions event at Bellewstown on her most recent outing, she handles today's trip but returns from a layoff of around nine months and faces a strong field. Considerably more needed to make an impact at this level.

runners_data.name: Dreamkeeper
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's 3-year-old is the field's lightest-weighted runner (119lbs) and has won over 12f on good ground on her latest start, giving this trip and surface confirmation; she is a natural front-runner and Chris Hayes will send her forward — the clash with Counting Coup is the race's defining tactical battleground, and the bigger question is whether she can sustain that effort after a contested gallop.
runners_data.comment: Getting off the mark emphatically at Fairyhouse last time, she showed the ability to handle today's conditions at this trip, but requires significant further development to make an impact in much stronger company.

races.paceDynamic: Counting Coup and Dreamkeeper are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 1m4f trip, creating a genuine, honest gallop on good ground at Roscommon. Counting Coup, fresh off a win 10 days ago, will push for the front rail, while Dreamkeeper — carrying a featherweight 119lbs as the sole 3-year-old — will be equally aggressive under Chris Hayes, ensuring neither can bowl along unchallenged. The resulting pace is likely to be true and sustained, which on good ground over this distance classically stretches the field and favours horses who can travel smoothly in behind before delivering a measured late effort — making the prominent-to-midfield stalker the most advantaged profile. Bosphorus Rose and Abbey Actress are true prominent racers who are unlikely to secure their natural position in a field that already has Chally Chute, Starford and Shaool occupying the principal prominent slots; Chally Chute and Starford, with their superior ORs and course-form, are the likeliest to establish those berths.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Stalkers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Counting Coup and Dreamkeeper set a genuine, pressed gallop that stretches the field from the first half-mile.
scenarios.body: If Counting Coup and Dreamkeeper set a genuine, pressed gallop that stretches the field from the first half-mile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Gallops Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner (most likely Counting Coup) edges the contest for the lead and is allowed to dictate at a measured, uncontested tempo.
scenarios.body: If one front-runner (most likely Counting Coup) edges the contest for the lead and is allowed to dictate at a measured, uncontested tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Class Comes From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to soften the leaders and the higher-rated horses midfield produce a decisive run in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to soften the leaders and the higher-rated horses midfield produce a decisive run in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace implodes or collapses dramatically and the field concertinas, allowing a late run from deep to get to the line.
scenarios.body: If the pace implodes or collapses dramatically and the field concertinas, allowing a late run from deep to get to the line.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Counting Coup or Dreamkeeper seizes a clear early lead at the start — if one edges ahead unchallenged in the first two furlongs, the race shape shifts markedly toward Scenario B.

Bosphorus Rose and Abbey Actress are true prominent horses who will be forced wider and further back than natural — watch their position at the first bend; if either slots in closer than expected, their chance improves significantly beyond their STYLE_FIT discount.

Kalixa is 271 days absent and her trainer is 0/13 in the past 14 days — watch the market for any unusual support, which could indicate a stable confidence play, though form analysis alone warrants caution.

Starford's 53-day absence for Joseph O'Brien is worth monitoring in the betting; the McMonagle booking is a positive signal and O'Brien horses often arrive fresh but fit — any market move here is meaningful.
The going has been consistently Good across all reported races at Roscommon tonight including both runs over 1m4f, confirming a true, reliable surface with no hidden variance to distort the pace map.

races.name: Ladies Day At Roscommon On Monday, 6th July, 2026 Maiden

runners_data.name: Black Heather
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's 7-year-old returns from 451 days off (360 since jockey ride) with solid good-ground form at big distances, but is a natural rear-of-field operator whose true hold-up style places her among horses she would normally be finishing past, not racing alongside — the congested hold-up group makes a clean run from the back genuinely difficult here.
runners_data.comment: Effective at 12f on a sound surface, he has the profile for the trip and conditions here. Returns from an extended absence after a hurdle exit at Bellewstown, so the layoff is the main concern, but he is respected as a threat.

runners_data.name: Coolnagrattan
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 4-year-old for W R Crawford with only one career run on good ground — that was fourth over 2m, so stamina is not in doubt, but the absence of any racecourse experience at this trip and open maiden form make this a projection rather than a known quantity.
runners_data.comment: Showed a degree of encouragement in his bumper debut at Punchestown, finishing fourth while wearing first-time hood and tongue-tie, but will need considerably more on his Flat debut to make an impression here.

runners_data.name: Cracking Cloud
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's consistent 4-year-old has placed at shorter trips and arrives 29 days fresh, but a step up to 1m4f from 10f is a clear stamina question — the prominent style is well suited to tracking Boujee if the legs hold out.
runners_data.comment: Having shown fair ability at around 9f on today's going, he looks interesting now stepping up to 12f for the first time. Beaten seven lengths at Gowran Park last time, he is winless in recent starts but the longer trip could bring out more.

runners_data.name: Double Indian
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's entry carries a fade-in-finish flag across its form history and has only one run at this distance (13th on good); the hold-up style and tendency to weaken late make this a difficult profile to recommend in a race with a slow-turning pace.
runners_data.comment: His only start came in a bumper at Kilbeggan where he was well beaten, and a Flat debut off a short break leaves plenty to prove. The yard's involvement is a small positive, but he faces a stiff task here.

runners_data.name: Elman
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's 4-year-old is essentially a hold-up type whose recent form string (740-0) offers little encouragement, and the best of his limited good-ground experience is at 16f — his true rear-of-field style is buried in a midfield position here, compounding an already thin winning case.
runners_data.comment: Carries first-time tongue-tie on his return from a short break, having fallen in a maiden hurdle at Limerick most recently when already well beaten. He has questions to answer stepping back onto the Flat, though he has some rated ability to call on.

runners_data.name: It's Good To Talk
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins's 5-year-old has back-to-back finishing positions of 11th and 12th over 10f on good ground, then a fair 2nd over 16f in heavy, which at least confirms stamina; the fade flag and hold-up style are a concern when pace is expected to be controlled rather than generous.
runners_data.comment: Twice unplaced in recent outings, including at Gowran Park last month, without offering much encouragement in either start. His figures leave him with little margin for error and it is difficult to construct a strong case.

runners_data.name: Lauro's Legend
runners_data.note: P A Fahy's 6-year-old ran just 12 days ago (7th over 15f on good), has decent stamina credentials at these distances, but the fade-in-finish flag is a recurring issue and his hold-up style will leave him reliant on others setting an honest gallop — which Boujee alone cannot guarantee.
runners_data.comment: On his Flat debut at Leopardstown he was beaten nine lengths at a shorter trip, though his pedigree suggests the further stamina test of 15f suits him best. He may need the experience, but the step up in distance could eventually play to his strengths.

runners_data.name: Quint Major
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old for M A Molloy absent 264 days (228 since jockey), with one win from 15 career runs on good ground over this distance band — the hold-up style and lengthy break make this very speculative, though the course experience is the one positive.
runners_data.comment: His most recent effort came in a hurdle on very testing ground where he was never a factor, but that run may not reflect his true ability on a sounder surface. Respected on returning to the Flat, where he handles today's conditions and has the stamina to stay this trip and further.

runners_data.name: Seti One
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's 4-year-old has a fade flag, a form string of 84000-, and a racing style that is genuinely rear-of-field — pushed into midfield by the redistribution, he cannot express his natural game and his Flat form on good ground is slender at best.
runners_data.comment: Lightly tried at today's course and distance with form showing he handles cut in the ground, he returns from a lengthy absence having finished well down the field at Dundalk most recently. He can show improvement on his day, though inconsistency remains a concern.

runners_data.name: Steel Cut
runners_data.note: A Oliver's 4-year-old wears a hood and has placed second over 10f on standard, travelling 10 days fresh — the prominent style is exactly what this race shape rewards behind Boujee, and the headgear suggests a focused effort; the step up to 1m4f from 10f is the key fitness question.
runners_data.comment: Held at Down Royal last time but effective over today's distance and conditions, he attracts a top jockey and lines up in first-time blinkers, which could sharpen the response. He has the ability to make his presence felt here.

runners_data.name: Ashikita
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's 5-year-old (Ben Coen aboard) ran 27 days ago and showed a shade of form (5th over 12f on good) but is fundamentally a hold-up type — the redistribution pushes her forward into midfield against her grain, and with the pace expected to be modest rather than searching, her finishing effort may simply arrive too late.
runners_data.comment: After an unplaced debut, she took a step forward at the Curragh last time, finishing fifth and shaping with credit over today's 12f trip. The trainer is in strong current form and she looks well placed to go well in this modest field.

runners_data.name: Boujee
runners_data.note: M A Molloy's 9-year-old is the lone confirmed front-runner but has been absent 335 days (jockey only 25 days), which is a material fitness risk over 1m4f; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) notes she is slightly off-role as a nominal prominent type, and the race shape is hers to control — the durability of that control in the final stages is the critical question.
runners_data.comment: Her latest effort ended early in a hurdle at Clonmel, and returning to the Flat after that exit leaves a number of questions to answer. She has shown more in bumpers before but faces a stiff task here on these figures.

runners_data.name: Catherine Magennis
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride for Joseph Murphy on this lightly raced 4-year-old who has only a single start (7th over 10f on soft) on record — the jockey is a significant booking for a one-run maiden, but there is almost no evidence on which to base a distance or going assessment.
runners_data.comment: Showed encouragement on her debut at Gowran Park despite finishing seventh and well beaten, and she returns from an absence of around three months with form suggesting she handles soft ground best over shorter. Improvement needed stepping up to 12f today.

runners_data.name: Grennanstown Lady
runners_data.note: Gerard Keane's 5-year-old has reasonable staying form with a 4th and 5th over 18f on good ground and arrives 56 days since last run (21 since jockey) — the hold-up style is her natural mode, and while her form fits the distance, she needs either a proper pace or a clear run inside the final two furlongs.
runners_data.comment: She was outrun and never a factor in a hurdle at Sligo most recently, and it is hard to see a route back to competitiveness on the Flat from that display. Difficult to recommend on her current figures.

runners_data.name: Sioux Grit
runners_data.note: R P Burns's 8-year-old returns from 773 days off the track with form that reads 5/000/ — a natural hold-up type mapped to midfield by redistribution, the combination of extreme absence, a fade flag, and rock-bottom OR of 32 makes a winning contribution almost impossible to envisage here.
runners_data.comment: Returning from an absence of well over two years, she has been running at a consistently poor level in recent starts and was down the field at Navan last time. Faces a considerable task from a mark of 32 on this comeback.

runners_data.name: Taj Crown
runners_data.note: K J Condon's 4-year-old (Ronan Whelan) wears a visor and ran 11 days ago (8th over 12f on soft, but 2nd over 12f on good previously) — the prominent style is directly relevant to this pace map, the visor sharpens focus, and the good-ground second suggests the going suits; a step to 1m4f is likely within reach.
runners_data.comment: Uncharacteristically well beaten at Limerick last time after a sequence of more encouraging form, she now tries a first-time visor and handles today's distance and conditions well. There could be more to offer if she returns to her better level.

races.paceDynamic: Boujee is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-runner maiden over 1m4f on good ground at Roscommon, and with no identified rival willing or able to contest the lead, she is set to dictate a controlled, uncontested gallop from the front. Steel Cut, Cracking Cloud and Taj Crown are the nearest prominent types and will likely track Boujee in the early stages, but none carries the profile to force a genuine test on the leader. With the pace sustainable rather than pressured, the race is likely to develop into a mid-race cruise before a steadier finish-line sprint, which tilts the tactical advantage firmly toward horses who can sit close to the pace and quicken over the last two furlongs — prominent racers and handy midfielders are best placed, while true hold-up horses face an uphill task producing their finish against a compressed field. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the map can honestly place at the rear — Black Heather, Ashikita, Seti One, Elman and Sioux Grit are all genuine closers who will be shuffled into midfield positions they do not naturally want, meaning their finishing kicks may arrive too late off a slow-turning pace.

scenarios.title: Boujee Leads, Prompt Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Boujee controls an uncontested lead throughout and the race is decided by those tracking her from prominent positions.
scenarios.body: If Boujee controls an uncontested lead throughout and the race is decided by those tracking her from prominent positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Fades Late
scenarios.trigger: If Boujee's long absence (335 days since last run, 25 days since jockey last rode) catches up and she weakens in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: If Boujee's long absence (335 days since last run, 25 days since jockey last rode) catches up and she weakens in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late enough to create a proper gaps-opening finish and a genuine closer manages to thread a path.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses late enough to create a proper gaps-opening finish and a genuine closer manages to thread a path.

scenarios.title: Pace Lifts, Strong Stayer Wins
scenarios.trigger: If a runner with genuine stamina reserves proves superior when a faster-than-expected pace is injected by the prominent types chasing Boujee.
scenarios.body: If a runner with genuine stamina reserves proves superior when a faster-than-expected pace is injected by the prominent types chasing Boujee.

watchPoints.text: Boujee's 335-day absence is the dominant risk factor — if she weakens sharply after the half-mile marker rather than just the final furlong, the race could collapse into chaos behind her with Steel Cut and Taj Crown scrambling to fill the space.

Steel Cut (hood, 10 days fresh) and Taj Crown (visor, 11 days) both wear headgear that suggests they can be lit up in the early stages — if either chases Boujee harder than expected and turns this into a more genuine gallop, hold-up horses may get a fairer test than the pace map implies.

The sheer density of hold-up horses redistributed into midfield — Black Heather, Ashikita, Elman, Seti One, Sioux Grit — creates a significant traffic risk in the straight; watch for a logjam as multiple hold-up types simultaneously request a gap that does not exist.

Coolnagrattan's single career run was over 2m on good ground in a bumper-adjacent context — Seamie Heffernan takes the ride for a lightly raced yard, and any improvement from experience could be substantial on a step back to 1m4f.

Catherine Magennis has attracted Dylan Browne McMonagle despite having only one career start — monitor market movement at the off, as the jockey booking is disproportionately strong for a horse with almost no public form.
